summary: Branch SD-WAN split-tunnel DNS bypass causes OCSP lookup latency and intermittent gRPC idle resets
description:
Issue summary: BrightPay reports intermittent slow model starts and periodic gRPC idle resets for their private deployment after they enabled a branch office SD-WAN with split-tunnel DNS forwarding. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints show increased 1xx/5xx retries and occasional client-observed request timeouts during morning batch windows. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC with VPCE to Redwood control plane), multiple branch offices using SD-WAN CPE devices configured to forward DNS for internal names to a corporate resolver and all other DNS to Internet.

Observed behavior: Serving nodes experience long TLS handshakes (1.5-3s) toward Redwood control plane OCSP responder and occasional gRPC IDLE resets causing KV cache recompute. Customer saw spike in ephemeral ports and conntrack shortfalls on their NAT gateway while the SD-WAN CPE alternately forwarded DNS to corporate resolver then to ISP resolver causing DNS answer oscillation and transient NXDOMAINs for Redwood VPCE aliases.

Why it's customer-impacting: certificate revocation/OCSP checks and SNI name verification on presigned artifact fetches are sensitive to DNS resolution ordering; when DNS alternates, TLS stalls waiting on OCSP stapling and gRPC backpressure triggers idle connection tear-downs and token refresh failures for long-lived streams.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy private agent with VPCE and configure branch SD-WAN split-tunnel: internal FQDNs -> corp-dns, all else -> ISP resolver.
2) Configure SD-WAN CPE to prioritize corp-dns but enable fallback to ISP resolver on NXDOMAIN.
3) Trigger large nightly model shard fetch and parallel inference requests from branch office.
4) Observe control-plane TLS handshake time and gRPC stream stability metrics in Console (per-route latency, streaming errors).
observed_logs_and_snippets:
- Agent logs (serving-node-02): TLS handshake to control-plane-ocsp.redwood.internal: elapsed=2124ms, reason=OCSP-lookup-timeout
- Agent stdout: grpc: stream: idle timeout after 65s, resetting connection
- NAT gw conntrack: ephemeral ports 32768-61000 exhausted transiently during batch start (approx 78k conntrack entries)
- tcpdump from branch CPE: repeated DNS queries for vpce-redwood.prod.example.com -> alternating responses: 10.0.4.22 (corp) then 203.0.113.44 (isp) with differing CNAME chain
- curl --resolve against vpce alias: TLS handshake stalls while waiting for OCSP staple (OCSP responder probe shows 504 from corp-resolver path)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - Support: Initial triage, confirmed increased TLS handshake latencies and gRPC resets from customer's serving nodes. Asked for packet captures and NAT/conntrack metrics.

2026-03-10 11:05 UTC - Customer: Provided tcpdump from branch CPE and NAT gateway conntrack snapshots. Noted that issue correlates with SD-WAN reconvergence windows (every 5-7 minutes during morning sync).

2026-03-10 13:40 UTC - SRE (Rafael): Reproduced DNS oscillation locally by configuring dual resolvers with different CNAME responses. Observed OCSP lookup followed by retry to second resolver resulted in missing OCSP staple causing handshake plateau at ~1.8s. Hypothesis: split-tunnel fallback order plus corp-dns negative caching causes transient NXDOMAIN/incorrect CNAME leading to OCSP responder misrouting and TLS delay.

2026-03-11 02:15 UTC - SRE: Confirmed conntrack exhaustion at NAT layer exacerbates symptom; ephemeral port reuse causes presigned URL range downloads to fail mid-range leading to model shard fetch retries and higher token churn. Suggested mitigations: adjust SD-WAN DNS rule to always return canonical vpce alias, increase NAT conntrack, and pin control-plane endpoints in agent host file as interim.

2026-03-11 14:00 UTC - Engineering: Reviewed agent behavior for OCSP lookup path; found short-circuit fallback to second resolver without honoring negative TTL leads to rapid retries. Created task to add exponential backoff for OCSP DNS lookups in agent codebase.
customer_communication_log: 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Maya Chen (Support) to BrightPay: Thanks for the packet captures. We're triaging and will loop in SRE to look at OCSP and DNS ordering. Please include NAT/conntrack snapshots for the branch gateways.
2026-03-10 12:00 UTC - BrightPay (Raj Patel): Uploaded NAT snapshots and confirmed SD-WAN reconverges every ~6 minutes during morning sync. We see spikes in user-facing latency then. Any workaround?

2026-03-11 03:00 UTC - Rafael Ortega (SRE) to BrightPay: Short-term workaround: update SD-WAN DNS policy to prefer ISP resolver for VPCE aliases (so canonical CNAME path is consistent) or add static /etc/hosts entry on serving nodes for the VPCE alias to guarantee consistent resolution. We'll propose longer-term agent fix.

2026-03-11 15:20 UTC - BrightPay (Raj Patel): Applied hostfile pinning on three serving nodes and saw TLS handshake median reduce from 1.9s -> 120ms and gRPC resets drop by 92% during next morning window. Customer requests official remediation plan before closing.
actions_taken:
- Provided immediate mitigation options: 1) pin VPCE alias in /etc/hosts on serving nodes, 2) change SD-WAN DNS split-tunnel rule to avoid alternating resolvers for Redwood VPCE names, 3) increase NAT conntrack table size on branch gateways.
- Eng created a code task to add exponential backoff and negative-ttl respect to agent OCSP DNS lookup path (tracked by GH PR linked).
- SRE recommended a scheduled change window for BrightPay to test SD-WAN rule change and to monitor per-route streaming metrics in Console.
resolution: Partial workaround validated by customer: /etc/hosts pinning produced immediate improvement and reduced errors. Long-term fix pending: engineering will land agent change to respect negative TTLs and exponential backoff on OCSP DNS lookups to avoid rapid failover-induced stalls. Customer agreed to a change window for SD-WAN DNS policy next week. Ticket remains 'In Progress' until PR lands and SD-WAN change validated.
postmortem_followup_items: ENG-687: Add negative-ttl honoring and exponential backoff to OCSP DNS path in private-agent (owner: infra-agent-team).
OPS-142: Add a KB article in Console docs: 'SD-WAN split-tunnel recommendations for Redwood Private deployments' with explicit DNS rules to avoid alternating resolvers for VPCE aliases.
SUP-TRACK-11: Outreach to top private-tier customers with SD-WAN deployments to recommend mitigations and diagnostic checklist.
